items.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995
items.q: And we have Louie Bellson comes and plays with them, and Joe’s done concerts with them.

ctx.x: A cappella. And there are about eight or a dozen of them. They are terrific. They’re called the something sounds, I’ve forgot. I shouldn’t have brought it up if I can’t remember the name but I don’t remember the name. They are marvelous. And Joe says as long as there are kids making that kind of sound there is certainly hope. And there’s a singer at a college in Colorado, who used to be there, I suppose he’s graduated now, who did a wonderful imitation of Joe singing, could have been Joe, we had a tape of it. He…

I think they mentioned, the two of them this morning, some of the big differences. There’s a lot of the young musicians who spend a lot of time in colleges and learn very technically and so forth, and they have to learn what to do with it later on. Which in the earlier days, when people were mostly listening from records and then getting into the situations and playing in the traveling bands, that hearing things was—either you developed it or you were gone.
